title: Does the Multilingual 'Universal Feature' Finding Hold in Small Open Models?

original_idea.body: On an open multilingual model, test whether the same residual direction/SAE latent for a concept activates across languages via cosine similarity and cross-lingual patching.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cross-lingual feature sharing informs whether safety interventions transfer across languages, plausible but with a gap (level 3).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Concept identification + cross-lingual patching on an open multilingual model; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable with multilingual data dependency (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, externally runnable multilingual-safety replication (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Small open multilingual models, inference-only; CPU/light-GPU feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Cross-lingual features shown at frontier; small-model replication partly open; partially addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Small-model cross-lingual replication may be partly open.
